**Answer: 673 CHIP variants remain after removing reference calls.**

Counting rule (one sentence): keying every row in the 86 sample workbooks on (Chr:Pos, Ref/Alt) and dropping reference calls (Zygosity = 'Reference'; blank zygosity treated as no-call), 673 distinct variants are genotyped as Heterozygous or Homozygous Variant in at least one sample.

Full executed results (script: analysis_chip_variants.py, log/results in out/):
- Files loaded: 86; variant data rows (after the 2 merged header rows): 57,258
- Zygosity row breakdown: Reference 44,211 | Heterozygous 7,303 | Homozygous Variant 4,593 | blank/no-call 1,151
- Total distinct (Chr:Pos, Ref/Alt) keys before removal: 707 (701 distinct positions)
- Keys never alt-called (Reference and/or blank only): 34 (of which 8 are Reference-only in every sample)
- **Primary count — distinct variants with ≥1 alt (Het/HomVar) call: 673** (673 distinct positions; no position carries two retained alt alleles)
- Per-sample alt-call rows: 11,896
- Sensitivity, strict 56-gene-list membership: 627 distinct alt-called keys (the primary 673 includes 46 keys annotated to non-list neighbors such as MMAB/MMACHC/SF3B2 or antisense transcripts like TET2-AS1; per the approved plan the primary count uses the pre-filtered workbook rows, all of which carry In_CHIP=True)

Most frequent genes among retained variants: NOTCH1 (48), CUX1 (36), MMAB (35), JAK3 (27), PDGFRA (23), FLT3 (23), TET2 (20), GNAS (19), ASXL1 (19), SMC3 (19).

payload.counting_rule: Distinct (Chr:Pos, Ref/Alt) keys genotyped Heterozygous or Homozygous Variant in at least one of the 86 sample workbooks, after removing Zygosity='Reference' rows (blank = no-call).
